Three-day croissant process, written out after batch 9 (Jan 2025) finally gave a proper honeycomb. Before that, eight batches of bread rolls with ambitions.

## Détrempe (the dough)

For 12 croissants:

- 500 g T45 flour (Wessex Mill French-style, £2.40/1.5 kg)
- 55 g caster sugar
- 10 g salt
- 7 g instant yeast (or 5 g yeast + 75 g of the levain from [[Yeast water starter]])
- 140 g cold milk + 140 g cold water
- 40 g soft butter

Mix 4 min on low on the Kenwood, no more. Don't develop it, you want it slack. Flatten to a 2 cm slab, wrap, fridge overnight at 4°C.

## Butter block

280 g Lescure 82% fat butter (£6.90 at Waitrose, the English 80% stuff is too wet). Bash it between parchment with a rolling pin into a 17 x 17 cm slab, 1 cm thick. Fridge 30 min, then out for 10 min before using. Target: butter and dough both at about 10 to 12°C and the same bend. Butter cracks if colder, smears if warmer.

## Lock-in

Roll the dough to 34 x 17. Butter on one half, dough over it, pinch the edges. Turn 90 degrees.

## Turns

- 1 double turn (book turn): roll to 60 cm long, 6 mm thick, ends to the middle, then in half
- fridge 30 min
- 1 single turn (letter turn): roll to 45 cm, in thirds
- fridge 1 hour minimum
- that's 12 butter layers from a double and a single, 4 x 3. Tried double + double (16) in batch 6, too fine, it went bready.

Fridge temp matters. The commissary walk-in is 3°C, the truck fridge is 6°C. Use the walk-in.

## Shaping

Roll to 4 mm, 25 cm wide. Triangles 9 cm base, 25 cm tall, about 80 g each. Small nick at the base, roll up with a light hand, tip underneath. 12 croissants and 4 offcut pains suisses.

## Proof

26°C and humid, in the Brød & Taylor box with a tray of water, 2.5 to 3 hours. Above 28°C the butter leaks out and you get a puddle. Ready when they wobble like jelly when you shake the tray and the layers are visible from the side. Egg wash (1 yolk, 1 tbsp milk, pinch salt) twice, before and after the last 30 min.

## Bake

- 190°C fan, 18 to 20 min
- that's 190 on the probe. The truck Lincat reads 17 degrees under, setting it to 175 gives 190 ([[Oven thermometer calibration]])
- rotate tray at 10 min
- deep brown, not golden. Golden is underbaked, the inside will be doughy

## Failures log

- batch 2 (Oct 2024): butter too cold, shattered into plates, patchy layers
- batch 4: proof at 30°C, butter pool on the tray, 140 g of butter lost
- batch 6: too many turns, see above
- batch 7: oven at "190" was actually 207, black bottoms and raw middles, which is what made me buy the thermometers
- batch 9 (14 Jan 2025): honeycomb. Cut one in half and photographed it for Tash.

## Costing

Per croissant: £0.71 ingredients. Sold at £3.20 at the [[Bake sale 2025 notes]] and gone in 40 min. Truck can't make them daily, the lamination takes 2.5 hours of hands-on time on top of the overnight rests.

## Next
